text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.59% today, continuing a sharp three-day rally that has recovered most of last week's losses. The stock has climbed $5.69 (4.4%) since November 10th, tracking closely with oil prices, which have stabilized around $89–$92 per barrel after earlier weakness. The heating oil price surge reported today (up 59% year-over-year) signals strong demand in the fuel sector heading into winter, which can support crude and refined product margins for integrated energy companies like ConocoPhillips.

The broader context: while Russia's crude production rebound has pushed global oil into surplus according to the IEA, the U.S. market appears to be holding its own on the strength of seasonal heating demand and refining needs. This creates a tug-of-war — oversupply pressure from abroad tempered by real winter-season demand at home — which may explain why the stock has bounced rather than collapsed despite the international supply news.
